title: incident-bot: oncall autodiagnostics quicklinks + runbook prioritization
author: Jordan Liu
body:
Motivation: On recent incidents oncall responders lost time hunting for the most relevant runbook sections. This change surfaces quicklinks and a lightweight prioritization score in autodiagnostics so responders land on the most likely remediation steps faster.

What this PR does: Adds quicklink generation to the autodiagnostics pipeline, computes a runbook relevance score (SLO match, recent-success signals, error fingerprint overlap), surfaces top-3 runbook anchors in the Slack oncall message + incident-bot web UI, and adds telemetry (runbook_click, runbook_suggest_score) to measure effectiveness. Also includes an opt-in rollout flag, unit+integration tests for the prioritization heuristics, and migration for stored runbook metadata.

Implementation notes: Relevance score is a weighted sum of: SLO alignment (50%), recent success (20%), error fingerprint overlap (20%), and manual priority override (10%). We keep offline-safe defaults so the system gracefully degrades to original quicklinks when signals are missing. Quicklinks are generated from runbook anchors annotated in markdown (--- anchor: <id> ), and we added a small parser in incident-bot/runbooks/anchors.py.

Rollout plan: Feature flagged behind rollout:autodiag_runbook_quicklinks; start with 5% of incidents for SRE teams, monitor click-through and time-to-ack. If metrics regress, we will rollback via the feature flag.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for anchor parser and scoring - [x] Integration tests for message formatting - [x] Telemetry events wired - [x] Feature flag + 5% rollout - [x] Docs changes (runbooks + ops playbooks) - [x] Added SRE review

Related: Linear ENG-2345 (oncall autodiagnostics improvements), ENG-2380 (runbook metadata migration).

review_comments:
Aisha Patel: Can we make the default weights configurable per-organization? I worry about one-size-fits-all.
Jordan Liu: Added feature flag + org-level weights option; defaults preserve existing behavior.

Roberto Garcia: Slack message looks a bit verbose on small pager devices. Can we collapse anchors into a single expandable block?
Jordan Liu: Updated slack formatter to use a collapsed block with a visible top-3 and an expand link for full anchors.

Mei Chen: Add a migration note for runbook metadata stored in Redis.
Jordan Liu: Added migration helper (incident-bot/migrations/20260212_runbook_meta_migrate.py) and documented the steps in the PR body.
release_notes: Adds runbook quicklinks and relevance scoring to autodiagnostics; opt-in feature flag and metrics for rollout.
